sections.question: Can tourists buy weed in Seattle?
sections.short: Yes. You don’t need to be a Washington resident: anyone 21 or older with a valid government-issued ID can buy at a state-licensed retail store.

points.text: You do not need to be a Washington resident to buy cannabis, but you must be 21 or older and show a valid government-issued ID.
Cannabis may be sold only at state-licensed stores. People under 21 are not allowed inside, and many stores accept cash only.
Visitors 21 and older may buy at a licensed store, and should use or dispose of their cannabis before leaving the state.

sections.question: How do I find a licensed cannabis store in Seattle?
sections.short: Use the Liquor and Cannabis Board’s map of licensed retailers. If you aren’t sure a store is licensed, you can ask to see its LCB-issued license.

points.text: The Liquor and Cannabis Board publishes a map of licensed cannabis retailers.

link.label: Find a licensed store on the Liquor and Cannabis Board’s map

points.text: If you are not sure a location is licensed, you can ask to see its LCB-issued license.
Adult-use cannabis must be bought from a state-licensed retail store.

sections.question: How much weed can I have in Washington?
sections.short: Up to 1 ounce of cannabis flower. Edibles, liquids and concentrates have their own limits: 16 ounces of solid edibles, 72 ounces of infused liquids and 7 grams of concentrate.

points.text: Adults 21 and older may have up to 1 ounce of cannabis plant matter, 16 ounces of solid cannabis-infused edibles, 72 ounces of cannabis-infused liquids and 7 grams of cannabis concentrate.
Only adults 21 and older may have or use adult-use cannabis.

sections.question: Where can you smoke weed in Seattle?
sections.short: Out of public view, where the property owner allows it. Opening a package of cannabis or using it in view of the public or in a public place is illegal, and that includes parks, sidewalks, restaurants, concerts and state and federal parks.

points.text: It is unlawful to open a package of cannabis or a cannabis product, or to consume it, in view of the general public or in a public place. It is a class 3 civil infraction.
The Liquor and Cannabis Board says the ban on public use covers places such as parks, sidewalks, restaurants, concerts and federal land, and that this includes state and federal parks.
Employers and landlords can set their own rules about cannabis.
Smoking, e-cigarettes included, is not allowed in Washington State Ferries terminals or on its vessels.

sections.question: Can I smoke weed in my Seattle hotel room?
sections.short: Only if the hotel allows it. The Liquor and Cannabis Board tells visitors to ask about a hotel’s policy before they go.

points.text: If you are visiting Washington, ask your hotel about its cannabis policy before your visit.
Check a hotel’s policy before using cannabis there.

sections.question: Is there a cannabis lounge in Seattle?
sections.short: No. Washington law makes it a felony to run a cannabis club, or any place open to the public where cannabis may be consumed.

points.text: It is unlawful to conduct or maintain a cannabis club, meaning a business with premises where cannabis is kept or consumed, or a public place where consuming cannabis is permitted. It is a class C felony.
Under that law, a public place includes any place that charges admission or is run for profit.

sections.question: Can I have weed in a car in Washington, or drive after using it?
sections.short: Keep it in its original sealed package, in the trunk or somewhere no one in the car can reach; the glove compartment doesn’t count. Driving high is illegal.

points.text: Cannabis in a vehicle must be in the trunk, or in an area the driver and passengers can’t reach, in its original package with the seal unbroken. The glove compartment is not acceptable.
It is illegal to drive under the influence of cannabis. A THC level of 5 nanograms or more within two hours of driving is a DUI, and you can be found guilty of DUI whatever a test shows.

sections.question: Can I take weed to Mount Rainier or Olympic National Park?
sections.short: No. Having or using any amount is prohibited in Mount Rainier National Park and the national forest land around it, and the Park Service says marijuana use is prohibited on federal land throughout Washington, Olympic National Park included.

points.text: Mount Rainier National Park says Washington’s law has no bearing on federal law, under which marijuana is a Schedule I drug. Possession or use of any amount is prohibited in the park, its facilities, concessions and campgrounds, and on the surrounding national forest land. Penalties can reach a $5,000 fine or six months in jail.
Olympic National Park reminds visitors that marijuana use is prohibited on federal lands within Washington, including Olympic National Park.
Cannabis can’t be used on federal property, national parks included.

sections.question: Can I fly home with weed from Seattle?
sections.short: No. It is illegal to take cannabis on a commercial aircraft, and illegal to take it out of Washington any other way, even to a state where it is legal. Use it or get rid of it before you leave.

points.text: It is illegal to take cannabis on a commercial aircraft.
It is illegal to take cannabis out of Washington, even to another state where it is legal, by plane, train, boat, car or any other way.
Visitors should use or dispose of their cannabis before leaving the state.

TSA says marijuana and some cannabis products, including some CBD oil, remain illegal under federal law unless they have no more than 0.3% THC on a dry-weight basis or are FDA-approved. Its officers don’t search for drugs, but they refer anything illegal they find to law enforcement.

sections.question: Does Washington accept medical cannabis cards from other states?
sections.short: No. A Washington medical cannabis patient must be a Washington resident, and the Department of Health says even someone moving to Washington can’t transfer patient status from another state. Visitors 21 and older can still buy at licensed stores.

points.text: A qualifying patient must be a Washington resident who has been diagnosed with a qualifying condition.
Someone who moves to Washington can’t transfer patient status from another state, the Department of Health says, because each state has different medical cannabis regulations.

sections.question: How much of an edible should I take?
sections.short: Start low and go slow. The Liquor and Cannabis Board suggests starting with 2 to 5 milligrams of THC, and an edible can take up to four hours for its full effect.

points.text: For edibles, start with a low amount of THC, such as 2 to 5 milligrams. You may need to cut an edible into halves or quarters.
Edibles can take up to four hours for their full effect.
